10.1002_adfm.202518076: Organic electrolyte additives have emerged as a promising strategy to regulate interfacial reactions at the Zn anode in aqueous batteries, yet their design remains largely empirical owing to a lack of molecular‐level understanding. In this work, a dual‐descriptor framework based on molecular polarizability and surface energy to guide the rational screening of electrolyte additives for stable Zn deposition is introduced. Systematic evaluation reveals that lower polarizability promotes the formation of a compact, water‐deficient electrical double layer (EDL), which enhances Zn 2+ desolvation and promotes rapid nucleation with oriented growth. Meanwhile, a moderately high surface energy, particularly when closely matched with that of the ZnSO 4 electrolyte, ensures stable interfacial adsorption and synergizes with low polarizability to achieve uniform Zn deposition. In contrast, excessively high surface energy induces additive aggregation, weakens EDL compactness, and leads to uneven deposition and parasitic side reactions. Guided by this dual‐descriptor screening framework, oxamide is identified as a representative additive featuring low polarizability and well‐matched surface energy. Its incorporation improves Zn deposition morphology, enhances coulombic efficiency, and delivers superior cycling stability in both half‐cell and Zn‐MnO 2 full‐cell configurations. This study demonstrates the effectiveness of descriptor‐guided additive design and offers a molecular‐level strategy for advancing stable and high‐performance aqueous Zn‐ion batteries.
10.1002_adfm.79052: Spin‐dependent pathways play a critical role in the oxygen evolution reaction (OER), yet direct and dynamic probing of spin‐selective catalysis remains challenging. Here we report an optical transduction strategy that provides a real‐time, chemically responsive readout of magnetically controlled spin‐selective OER. A ferrimagnetic Fe 3 O 4 /CoFe 2 O 4 heterointerface is engineered to establish a spin‐selective charge transport pathway, where interfacial magnetic coupling enables efficient field‐induced domain alignment under an external magnetic field. Electrochemical measurements and spin‐resolved calculations suggest that interfacial spin polarization favors triplet‐related oxygen evolution. Coupling this process to luminol electrochemiluminescence (ECL) translates changes in OER‐derived oxygen‐precursor availability into a reversible and peak‐selective optical signal through oxygen‐derived reactive species. The pronounced reverse‐scan enhancement provides a chemically amplified optical output of the magnetically regulated catalytic state, enabling dynamic optical transduction of spin‐dependent electrocatalysis. This work establishes a general framework for coupling spin‐dependent electrocatalysis with a chemically responsive optical readout, providing new opportunities for probing and controlling interfacial reactions through spin polarization.
10.1002_smll.202506912: Grid‐scale energy storage technologies are critical for stabilizing power grids increasingly reliant on intermittent renewable energy sources. Among these technologies, aqueous alkaline zinc‐ferricyanide flow batteries (AZFFBs) are promising candidates due to their low cost, high safety, and rapid kinetics. However, their practical deployment is hindered by the formation of “dead zinc”, which can cause irreversible capacity loss and block flow channels. Herein, we identify the growth of irreversible crystal buds as the primary cause of macroscopic zinc pulverization, which leads to “dead zinc” formation in AZFFBs. To address this issue, we introduce a multi‐coordination electrolyte additive, panthenol (PAN), which simultaneously coordinates with Zn(OH) 4 2− to homogenize ion transport at the electrode interface and promotes the formation and re‐atomization of reversible crystal buds. This strategy results in a 15‐fold increase in the cycling life of Zn||K 4 [Fe(CN) 6 ] full batteries, along with 2.1%, 3.1%, and 1.2% improvements in Coulombic efficiency, energy efficiency, and voltage efficiency, respectively. This work clarifies the formation mechanism of “dead zinc” in AZFFBs and proposes an efficient inhibition of zinc pulverization approach, bridging the gap between renewable energy generation and grid‐scale storage.
10.1021_acsami.5c21997: Wide-bandgap (WBG) perovskite solar cells (PSCs) based on self-assembled monolayers (SAMs) have demonstrated impressive efficiencies, though their performance and longevity remain substantially compromised by poor wettability during film formation, defects, and energy-level misalignment at the interfaces. Herein, we develop an interface regulation strategy employing a tris(4-carboxyphenyl)phosphine oxide (TC) modified [4-(7 H -benzimidazol-7-yl)butyl]phosphonic acid (4PADCB) to construct a multifunctional composite SAM (Co-SAM). The incorporation of TC molecules significantly enhances the interfacial wetting characteristics and crystallization quality of WBG perovskites, effectively passivating defects, optimizing energy-level alignment, and facilitating selective charge transport. This Co-SAM strategy yields impressive device performance: 1.68 eV WBG PSCs achieve a champion power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 22.40% while maintaining >90% of initial efficiency after 1440 h of ambient storage. Furthermore, perovskite/silicon tandem solar cells fabricated using this approach reach a PCE of 30.74%. Our work establishes a new paradigm in interfacial molecular engineering for highly efficient and operationally stable tandem photovoltaics.
10.1039_d6ee02519f: A strategy of dual active sites with distinct catalytic functions is proposed, thereby constructing a favorable hydrogenation microenvironment for efficient electrocatalytic O 2 -to-H 2 O 2 conversion at industrial-grade current densities.
